title: The rat and the snake
summary: "The Rat and the Snake" is a short story by A.E. van Vogt, a writer associated with the science fiction and fantasy magazines of the mid-twentieth century. The tale is set during a wartime period when rats have become scarce and costly to obtain. Mark Gray, a solitary man, keeps a pet python in a sealed room and amuses himself by feeding it rats through a rigged tunnel, savoring the sounds of their terror. When he discovers a research laboratory full of rats, he tries to steal some and is caught by its staff. The laboratory is secretly testing an experimental process on a human subject, and the story turns on a grim reversal of Mark's cruel pastime. The piece is brief and works as a sharp, ironic twist, examining cruelty, indifference and the moral blindness of people who see others as expendable. The text as supplied is a complete short piece, though it contains scattered OCR errors in places.
